mukta-m0-p01-v1.quick_english: Śiva, with parts and without parts, infinite, performs all effects through endless activity by his own will.

mukta-m0-p01-v2.quick_english: Śiva makes the variegated universe for the enjoyment of the enjoyers.

mukta-m0-p01-v3.quick_english: Just as a picture arises from its seed, so the variegated world arises not from a seed but from Śaṅkara.

mukta-m0-p01-v4.quick_english: What is seen and called a material cause, like thread, is unconscious.

mukta-m0-p01-v5.quick_english: Excluding the knowledge and action of the great lord, there is no cause.

mukta-m0-p01-v6.quick_english: And if the result comes from the actions of persons, what need is there here for the lord’s causation?

mukta-m0-p01-v7.quick_english: If action alone is accepted as producing effects, like ploughing and other actions, what else is to be inferred?

mukta-m0-p01-v8.quick_english: But like ploughing and other actions, it requires an intelligent agent.

mukta-m0-p01-v9.quick_english: When what is established is seen to be present, it is not proper to suppose an unseen cause.

mukta-m0-p01-v10.quick_english: If the seed could be by persons alone, what need is there for Hara? That is not so.

mukta-m0-p01-v11.quick_english: Therefore, the eternal production of effects beginning with kalā would follow.

mukta-m0-p01-v12.quick_english: Because of the mere existence of connection, when the production of causes and effects beginning with kalā occurs, the consequence would be non-liberation.

mukta-m0-p01-v13.quick_english: By whom is any effect ever seen anywhere to be accidental?

history.gloss: By whom is any effect ever seen anywhere to be accidental?

mukta-m0-p01-v14.quick_english: It is said that no effect is possible without an agent.

history.gloss: It is said that no effect is possible without an agent.

mukta-m0-p01-v15.quick_english: Therefore, in conjunction or in disjunction, the great lord is the cause of those two.

mukta-m0-p01-v16.quick_english: It is the supreme lord alone, and no other.

mukta-m0-p01-v17.quick_english: Even if you go far, you must still state that it is inherent nature alone.

mukta-m0-p01-v18.quick_english: Thus, much that is unseen will have to be imagined.

mukta-m0-p01-v19.quick_english: O wise ones, is activity that of one impelled by another, or of one who is independent?

mukta-m0-p01-v20.quick_english: Because an unconscious material cause is nowhere the independent maker of effects.

mukta-m0-p01-v21.quick_english: He who is the intelligent impeller of that is to be known as the lord.

mukta-m0-p01-v22.quick_english: It operates from whose intensity, in the daytime accompanied by night.

mukta-m0-p01-v23.quick_english: It operates from māyā, characterized by power, for the creation of the world; thus there is no other lord.

mukta-m0-p01-v24.quick_english: In that intensity, there is no cause other than the great lord.

mukta-m0-p01-v25.quick_english: Therefore, because any other explanation is impossible, only the supreme lord, endowed with supreme knowledge, is the cause of that intensification.

mukta-m0-p04-v76.quick_english: The individual self, being under the control of the great Lord, impurity, maya, and the rest, cannot by itself bring about its own liberation.

mukta-m0-p04-v77.quick_english: This self has no power for its own liberation, because it does not possess that power by itself.

mukta-m0-p04-v78.quick_english: Neither individual selves have the power to bring about liberation, nor do the bonds have such power.

mukta-m0-p04-v79.quick_english: Since Shiva alone is the remover of bondage, he alone is the giver of liberation to souls; when this is seen, there is no need to assume an unseen cause.

mukta-m0-p04-v80.quick_english: The bonds bring about the manifestation of knowing and doing in many different ways.

mukta-m0-p04-v81.quick_english: The bonds make that manifestation colored by their own form and inclined toward the functioning of bondage.

mukta-m0-p04-v82.quick_english: Impelled by worldly existence and because of their unconsciousness, the bonds bring about the manifestation of those two.

mukta-m0-p04-v83.quick_english: The power manifested by the bonds is called the knowing-and-doing power of the liberated.

mukta-m0-p04-v84.quick_english: Like that of a bound soul, when manifested by the bonds in the body and so on, it takes on attachment to grasping them as the self.

mukta-m0-p04-v85.quick_english: That power is not divided by bonds that arise or by bonds that are destroyed.

mukta-m0-p04-v86.quick_english: Even when the bonds dissolve, the liberated power abides in its own unchanged nature, just like the power of the Lord.

mukta-m0-p04-v87.quick_english: That power has all things as its scope and is therefore not of limited range.

mukta-m0-p04-v88.quick_english: It is not, like the power of a bound soul, sometimes limited to some particular object in some particular place.

mukta-m0-p04-v89.quick_english: And that power is not obstructed by another manifestation merely because another manifestation is absent.

mukta-m0-p04-v90.quick_english: The liberated power is not obstructed, because it is equal to Shiva and there is no further excellence beyond it.

mukta-m0-p04-v91.quick_english: The bonds do not manifest that power, nor is it ever overpowered by them again.

mukta-m0-p04-v92.quick_english: The manifestation of what is manifested would last only so long as the manifestor is present.

mukta-m0-p04-v93.quick_english: The Shaiva power that causes manifestation is that very state of proximity.

mukta-m0-p04-v94.quick_english: Thus, for that distinct liberated power, the bonds are not the cause.

mukta-m0-p04-v96.quick_english: Yoga, knowledge, austerity, and activity undertaken as a means to enjoyment.

mukta-m0-p04-v97.quick_english: The mind, because of its insentience.

mukta-m0-p04-v98.quick_english: Even very intense means do not by themselves cause the severing of one's own bondage.

mukta-m0-p04-v99.quick_english: Through connection with a special transformation, that may sometimes somehow occur for someone — thus verse 12.

mukta-m0-p04-v100.quick_english: But when the time of the authority of the obstructing power has passed, it happens of itself for the individual self.

mukta-m0-p01-v1.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v1.question: What nature enables Śiva to perform all effects by his own will?
premises: Śiva is described as with-parts and without-parts
Śiva is described as infinite
Śiva performs effects through endless activity by his own will
mukta-m0-p01-v1.inference: Śiva possesses a nature that encompasses all modes and enables autonomous action

mukta-m0-p01-v2.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v2.question: For whose sake and by whom is the variegated universe created?
premises: The universe is variegated
Enjoyers exist who experience the universe
Śiva makes the universe for their enjoyment
mukta-m0-p01-v2.inference: Śiva creates the diverse universe for the enjoyment of experiencing beings

mukta-m0-p01-v3.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v3.question: Does the variegated world arise from a material seed rather than from Śaṅkara?
premises: The world is compared to a variegated picture
A picture arises from a seed or material cause in the analogy
The world does not arise from such a seed but from Śaṅkara
mukta-m0-p01-v3.inference: The world’s origin is Śaṅkara, not a material seed like that of a picture
uncertainties: The exact force of citrād +bījān in the analogy is context-dependent

mukta-m0-p01-v4.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v4.question: What kind of material cause is observed in ordinary experience?
premises: A material cause is observed in experience
It is exemplified by thread
Such a material cause is unconscious
mukta-m0-p01-v4.inference: Observed material causes, like thread, are unconscious

mukta-m0-p01-v5.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v5.question: Can any cause be admitted while excluding the knowledge and action of the great lord?
premises: The great lord possesses knowledge and action
Excluding these leaves no adequate cause
No other cause can be established without them
mukta-m0-p01-v5.inference: The knowledge and action of the great lord cannot be excluded as the cause

mukta-m0-p01-v6.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v6.question: If results arise from the actions of persons, what need is there for the lord’s causation?
premises: Results are said to come from persons’ actions
This raises a question about the lord’s role
The necessity of the lord’s causation is challenged
mukta-m0-p01-v6.inference: The objection questions whether the lord’s causation is required beyond action

mukta-m0-p01-v7.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v7.question: If action alone produces effects like ploughing, why infer any other cause?
premises: Action is accepted as producing effects like ploughing
This suggests action alone is sufficient
The need for another inferred cause is questioned
mukta-m0-p01-v7.inference: The objection claims no further cause beyond action needs to be inferred

mukta-m0-p01-v8.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v8.question: Do actions like ploughing require an intelligent agent to produce their effects?
premises: Ploughing and similar actions produce effects
Such actions require an agent
The required agent must be intelligent
mukta-m0-p01-v8.inference: Effects like those of ploughing depend on an intelligent agent

mukta-m0-p01-v9.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v9.question: Is it reasonable to posit an unseen cause when an established cause is already observed?
premises: A cause may be established or yet to be established
When an observed cause is present, it accounts for the effect
Positing an unseen cause in that case is not proper
mukta-m0-p01-v9.inference: An unseen supposition is unwarranted when an observed cause suffices

mukta-m0-p01-v10.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v10.question: Can persons alone be the sufficient seed of the world without Hara’s role?
premises: It is suggested that persons alone could be the seed
This would exclude Hara as cause
Such exclusion is rejected
mukta-m0-p01-v10.inference: Persons alone cannot be the sufficient seed without Hara

mukta-m0-p01-v11.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v11.question: What undesirable consequence follows if no controlling lord governs the arising of effects like kalā?
premises: Effects beginning with kalā arise in the world
Without a controlling cause their arising would be unregulated
This would entail their eternal production
mukta-m0-p01-v11.inference: Denying a controlling lord leads to the absurdity of eternal production of effects

mukta-m0-p01-v12.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v12.question: Why would mere constant connection entail the consequence of non-liberation?
premises: If mere connection is sufficient, causes and effects would always operate
Effects beginning with kalā would continually arise
Continual arising would prevent liberation
mukta-m0-p01-v12.inference: Mere connection as cause leads to the consequence of non-liberation

mukta-m0-p01-v13.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v13.question: Is any effect ever observed to arise accidentally without a cause?
premises: Effects are observed in experience
No effect is observed to arise accidentally
This holds anywhere and for anything
mukta-m0-p01-v13.inference: Accidental arising of effects is not observed

mukta-m0-p01-v14.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v14.question: Can any effect be possible without an agent according to observation?
premises: Effects require conditions for their possibility
No effect is possible without an agent
This is stated as a general principle
mukta-m0-p01-v14.inference: An agentless effect is not possible

mukta-m0-p01-v15.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v15.question: Who is the cause of both conjunction and disjunction in the world?
premises: Conjunction and disjunction occur in the world
These require a governing cause
The great lord is that cause
mukta-m0-p01-v15.inference: The great lord is the cause of both conjunction and disjunction

mukta-m0-p01-v16.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v16.question: Is the supreme lord alone the ultimate cause, or is there another?
premises: A supreme cause is sought
The supreme lord is identified as that cause
No other is admitted as that cause
mukta-m0-p01-v16.inference: The supreme lord alone is the cause, not another

mukta-m0-p01-v17.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v17.question: Does appealing to inherent nature ultimately avoid positing a deeper cause?
premises: One may appeal to inherent nature as explanation
This appeal may be pushed far back
Even then inherent nature must be stated as the cause
mukta-m0-p01-v17.inference: Appealing to inherent nature does not eliminate the need for a stated cause

mukta-m0-p01-v18.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v18.question: What problem arises from explaining effects by positing many unseen factors?
premises: Explaining without a clear cause invites speculation
Many unseen factors may be imagined
Such imagination becomes excessive
mukta-m0-p01-v18.inference: Rejecting a proper cause leads to imagining many unseen factors

mukta-m0-p01-v19.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v19.question: Is activity properly attributed to what is impelled by another or to what is independent?
premises: Activity is observed in the world
Activity may belong to the dependent or the independent
The wise must determine which is the true source
mukta-m0-p01-v19.inference: The source of activity must be either a dependent or an independent agent

mukta-m0-p01-v20.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v20.question: Why cannot an unconscious material cause be the independent maker of effects?
premises: An unconscious material cause lacks autonomy
Making effects requires independence
An unconscious material cause is nowhere independent in producing effects
mukta-m0-p01-v20.inference: The independent maker of effects cannot be an unconscious material cause

mukta-m0-p01-v21.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v21.question: Who must be recognized as the intelligent impeller behind the material cause?
premises: An unconscious material cause requires an impeller
The impeller must be intelligent
That intelligent impeller is to be known as the lord
mukta-m0-p01-v21.inference: The lord is the intelligent impeller of the material cause

mukta-m0-p01-v22.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v22.question: What governs the operation of day and night through its varying intensity?
premises: Day and night operate in alternation
Their operation depends on a varying intensity
This intensity functions as the governing factor
mukta-m0-p01-v22.inference: The alternation of day and night proceeds from a governing intensity
uncertainties: The precise referent of yad +udrekād is determined by surrounding context

mukta-m0-p01-v23.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v23.question: Is the operative power for world-creation derived from māyā rather than from another lord?
premises: Creation of the world requires operative power
This power is characterized as arising from māyā
No other lord is the source of this operation
mukta-m0-p01-v23.inference: The power for world-creation operates from māyā and not from another lord
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sāmarthya +lakṣaṇān +māyāto is compact and interpretive

mukta-m0-p01-v24.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v24.question: What is the ultimate cause of that intensity if not the great lord?
premises: The intensity has a cause
No other cause is available
The great lord alone remains as its cause
mukta-m0-p01-v24.inference: There is no cause of that intensity other than the great lord

mukta-m0-p01-v25.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p01-v25.question: What establishes the supreme lord alone as the cause of that intensification?
premises: No cause other than the great lord exists for that intensification.
Any alternative explanation is impossible.
The supreme lord is endowed with excellence of knowledge.
mukta-m0-p01-v25.inference: Therefore, only the supreme lord endowed with excellence of knowledge is the cause of that intensification.
uncertainties: The exact referent of tasyāḥ is inferred from the preceding verse's discussion of intensification.

mukta-m0-p04-v76.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v76.question: Why can the individual self not liberate itself while under higher powers?
premises: The individual self is under the control of the great lord, impurity, maya, and others
Being under such control limits autonomous action
mukta-m0-p04-v76.inference: Therefore the individual self cannot achieve liberation by its own agency

mukta-m0-p04-v77.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v77.question: What capacity does the individual self lack regarding its own liberation?
premises: Liberation requires an effective power to remove bondage
The individual self does not possess such power by itself
mukta-m0-p04-v77.inference: Therefore the individual self has no power for its own liberation

mukta-m0-p04-v78.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v78.question: Do individual selves or the bonds possess the power to bring liberation?
premises: Individual selves lack liberating power
Bonds are insentient and cannot remove themselves
mukta-m0-p04-v78.inference: Therefore neither individual selves nor bonds have the power to effect liberation

mukta-m0-p04-v79.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v79.question: Who must be the giver of liberation if selves and bonds cannot remove bondage?
premises: Neither selves nor bonds can effect liberation
Shiva alone is the remover of bondage
When a visible cause is established, an unseen cause need not be assumed
mukta-m0-p04-v79.inference: Therefore Shiva alone is the giver of liberation to individual selves

mukta-m0-p04-v80.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v80.question: How do the bonds affect the manifestation of knowing and doing in the self?
premises: Knowing and doing are capacities of the self
Bonds condition how these capacities appear
mukta-m0-p04-v80.inference: Therefore the bonds produce the manifestation of knowing and doing in many ways

mukta-m0-p04-v81.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v81.question: In what manner do the bonds shape the manifested knowing and doing?
premises: Bonds impose their own character on manifestation
The resulting manifestation inclines toward bondage
mukta-m0-p04-v81.inference: Therefore the bonds make the manifestation colored by their own form and inclined to their functioning

mukta-m0-p04-v82.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v82.question: Why do the bonds produce the manifestation of knowing and doing in bound existence?
premises: Bonds are unconscious
Bonds are impelled by worldly existence
mukta-m0-p04-v82.inference: Therefore the bonds bring about the manifestation of knowing and doing without conscious intent

mukta-m0-p04-v83.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v83.question: How is the knowing-and-doing power characterized in relation to bonds and liberated selves?
premises: In ordinary states the power is manifested through bonds
In liberated selves the same power is identified as knowing and doing
mukta-m0-p04-v83.inference: Therefore the power manifested by bonds is called the knowing-and-doing power of the liberated

mukta-m0-p04-v84.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v84.question: What attachment arises when the self's power is manifested through bonds in the body?
premises: In the bound state the power is manifested by bonds
This manifestation occurs in the body and similar loci
mukta-m0-p04-v84.inference: Therefore, like a bound self, it takes on attachment to identifying with the body as self

mukta-m0-p04-v85.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v85.question: Does the arising or destruction of bonds alter the essential power of the self?
premises: Bonds may arise or be destroyed
The underlying power remains distinct from these changes
mukta-m0-p04-v85.inference: Therefore that power is not divided or altered by the arising or destruction of bonds

mukta-m0-p04-v86.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v86.question: Why does the liberated power remain unchanged even when the bonds dissolve?
premises: Bond dissolution removes limiting conditions
The liberated power abides in its own unchanged nature
It abides like the power of the Lord
mukta-m0-p04-v86.inference: Therefore the liberated power remains unchanged even in the dissolution of bonds

mukta-m0-p04-v87.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v87.question: What is the scope of the liberated power compared to a limited power?
premises: The liberated power is not restricted by bonds
A limited scope would imply bondage-like restriction
mukta-m0-p04-v87.inference: Therefore that power has all objects as its scope and is not of limited range

mukta-m0-p04-v88.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v88.question: How does the liberated power differ from the power of a bound self in scope?
premises: The power of a bound self is sometimes limited to some object in some place
The liberated power is not similarly restricted
mukta-m0-p04-v88.inference: Therefore the liberated power is not occasionally limited to some particular object like a bound self's power

mukta-m0-p04-v89.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v89.question: Is the liberated power obstructed by the absence of another manifestation?
premises: Obstruction would require a conflicting manifestation
In the liberated state no such conflicting manifestation arises
mukta-m0-p04-v89.inference: Therefore the liberated power is not obstructed by another manifestation merely due to its absence

mukta-m0-p04-v90.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v90.question: Why can the liberated power not be obstructed by any higher excellence?
premises: The liberated power is equal to Shiva
There is no further excellence beyond that equality
mukta-m0-p04-v90.inference: Therefore the liberated power is not obstructed because no higher excellence exists beyond it

mukta-m0-p04-v91.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v91.question: Can the bonds manifest or overpower the liberated power after liberation?
premises: Bonds no longer function as manifestors in the liberated state
The liberated power is not subject to renewed subjugation
mukta-m0-p04-v91.inference: Therefore the bonds neither manifest that power nor overpower it again

mukta-m0-p04-v92.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v92.question: Under what condition does a manifested manifestation depend on a manifestor?
premises: A manifested manifestation requires a manifesting condition
Such dependence lasts only while the manifestor is present
mukta-m0-p04-v92.inference: Therefore the manifestation of what is manifested lasts only as long as the manifestor is present

mukta-m0-p04-v93.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v93.question: What role does Shiva's power play in relation to the manifestor's proximity?
premises: Manifestation depends on a proximate manifesting cause
Shiva's power is the cause of manifestation
mukta-m0-p04-v93.inference: Therefore Shiva's power constitutes the proximity that brings about manifestation

mukta-m0-p04-v94.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v94.question: Why can the bonds not be the cause for the distinct liberated power?
premises: The liberated power is distinct in nature
Bonds function only in conditioned manifestation
mukta-m0-p04-v94.inference: Therefore the bonds are not the cause of that distinct liberated power

mukta-m0-p04-v95.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v95.question: What is being identified as the cause of liberation in this context?
premises: The preceding verses negate other causes
A true cause of liberation must be identified
mukta-m0-p04-v95.inference: Therefore the cause of liberation is being specified
uncertainties: This verse is a single token and may function as a heading or transition

mukta-m0-p04-v96.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v96.question: Which practices are considered as possible means related to liberation or experience?
premises: Yoga and knowledge are proposed as means
Austerity and activities aimed at enjoyment are also considered
mukta-m0-p04-v96.inference: Therefore yoga, knowledge, austerity, and activity for enjoyment are listed as candidate means

mukta-m0-p04-v97.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v97.question: Why is the mind insufficient as an ultimate liberating agent?
premises: The mind is insentient by nature
An insentient instrument cannot be the ultimate cause of liberation
mukta-m0-p04-v97.inference: Therefore the mind, being insentient, cannot be the ultimate liberating cause

mukta-m0-p04-v98.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p04-v98.question: Can even very intense practices sever the self from its bondage by themselves?
premises: Various means may be practiced intensely
Such means do not by themselves sever the self from bondage
mukta-m0-p04-v98.inference: Therefore even very intense means do not cause the severing of the self from bondage

mukta-m0-p01-v1.plain_english: Śiva, with parts and without parts, infinite, performs all effects through endless activity by his own will.

mukta-m0-p01-v2.plain_english: Śiva makes the variegated universe for the enjoyment of the enjoyers.
mukta-m0-p01-v2.sanskrit_cite: bhogināṃ bhuktaye viśvaṃ vicitraṃ kurute śivaḥ

mukta-m0-p01-v3.plain_english: Just as a picture arises from its seed, so the variegated world arises not from a seed but from Śaṅkara.

mukta-m0-p01-v4.plain_english: What is seen and called a material cause, like thread, is unconscious.

mukta-m0-p01-v5.plain_english: Excluding the knowledge and action of the great lord, there is no cause.

mukta-m0-p01-v6.plain_english: And if the result comes from the actions of persons, what need is there here for the lord’s causation?

mukta-m0-p01-v7.plain_english: If action alone is accepted as producing effects, like ploughing and other actions, what else is to be inferred?

mukta-m0-p01-v8.plain_english: But like ploughing and other actions, it requires an intelligent agent.

mukta-m0-p01-v9.plain_english: When what is established is seen to be present, it is not proper to suppose an unseen cause.
mukta-m0-p01-v9.sanskrit_cite: siddhasādhyatā tatra dṛṣṭe sati nādṛṣṭakalpanā yukteti

mukta-m0-p01-v10.plain_english: If the seed could be by persons alone, what need is there for Hara? That is not so.
mukta-m0-p01-v10.sanskrit_cite: pumbhireva bhaved bījaṃ kiṃ hareṇeti tannahi

mukta-m0-p01-v11.plain_english: Therefore, the eternal production of effects beginning with kalā would follow.

mukta-m0-p01-v12.plain_english: Because of the mere existence of connection, when the production of causes and effects beginning with kalā occurs, the consequence would be non-liberation.

mukta-m0-p01-v13.plain_english: By whom is any effect ever seen anywhere to be accidental?
mukta-m0-p01-v13.sanskrit_cite: yena nākasmikaṃ kāryaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kvacana kiñcana

mukta-m0-p01-v14.plain_english: It is said that no effect is possible without an agent.

mukta-m0-p01-v15.plain_english: Therefore, in conjunction or in disjunction, the great lord is the cause of those two.
mukta-m0-p01-v15.sanskrit_cite: tasmād yoge viyoge vā maheśaḥ kāraṇaṃ tayoḥ

mukta-m0-p01-v16.plain_english: It is the supreme lord alone, and no other.

mukta-m0-p01-v17.plain_english: Even if you go far, you must still state that it is inherent nature alone.
mukta-m0-p01-v17.sanskrit_cite: svabhāva eva vaktavyo gatvā dūramapi tvayā

mukta-m0-p01-v18.plain_english: Thus, much that is unseen will have to be imagined.

mukta-m0-p01-v19.plain_english: O wise ones, is activity that of one impelled by another, or of one who is independent?

mukta-m0-p01-v20.plain_english: Because an unconscious material cause is nowhere the independent maker of effects.

mukta-m0-p01-v21.plain_english: He who is the intelligent impeller of that is to be known as the lord.
mukta-m0-p01-v21.sanskrit_cite: prajñāvān prerakastasya yaḥ sa vijñeya īśvaraḥ

mukta-m0-p01-v22.plain_english: It operates from whose intensity, in the daytime accompanied by night.

mukta-m0-p01-v23.plain_english: It operates from māyā, characterized by power, for the creation of the world; thus there is no other lord.

mukta-m0-p01-v24.plain_english: In that intensity, there is no cause other than the great lord.

mukta-m0-p01-v25.plain_english: Therefore, because any other explanation is impossible, only the supreme lord, endowed with supreme knowledge, is the cause of that intensification.
mukta-m0-p01-v25.sanskrit_cite: ato'nyathānupapattyā jñānātiśayayuktaḥ parameśvara evodrede tasyāḥ kāraṇam

mukta-m0-p04-v76.plain_english: The individual self, being under the control of the great Lord, impurity, maya, and the rest, cannot by itself bring about its own liberation.

mukta-m0-p04-v77.plain_english: This self has no power for its own liberation, because it does not possess that power by itself.

mukta-m0-p04-v78.plain_english: Neither individual selves have the power to bring about liberation, nor do the bonds have such power.
mukta-m0-p04-v78.sanskrit_cite: na puṃsāṃ mocane śaktiḥ pāśānāmapi vidyate

mukta-m0-p04-v79.plain_english: Since Shiva alone is the remover of bondage, he alone is the giver of liberation to souls; when this is seen, there is no need to assume an unseen cause.
mukta-m0-p04-v79.sanskrit_cite: śiva eva tadā'pi nivartakatvāt puṃbhyo mokṣada iti dṛṣṭe sati nādṛṣṭakalpaneti

mukta-m0-p04-v80.plain_english: The bonds bring about the manifestation of knowing and doing in many different ways.

mukta-m0-p04-v81.plain_english: The bonds make that manifestation colored by their own form and inclined toward the functioning of bondage.

mukta-m0-p04-v82.plain_english: Impelled by worldly existence and because of their unconsciousness, the bonds bring about the manifestation of those two.

mukta-m0-p04-v83.plain_english: The power manifested by the bonds is called the knowing-and-doing power of the liberated.

mukta-m0-p04-v84.plain_english: Like that of a bound soul, when manifested by the bonds in the body and so on, it takes on attachment to grasping them as the self.

mukta-m0-p04-v85.plain_english: That power is not divided by bonds that arise or by bonds that are destroyed.
mukta-m0-p04-v85.sanskrit_cite: na cotpannairvinaṣṭairvā pāśaiḥ sā bhidyate yataḥ

mukta-m0-p04-v86.plain_english: Even when the bonds dissolve, the liberated power abides in its own unchanged nature, just like the power of the Lord.

mukta-m0-p04-v87.plain_english: That power has all things as its scope and is therefore not of limited range.

mukta-m0-p04-v88.plain_english: It is not, like the power of a bound soul, sometimes limited to some particular object in some particular place.

mukta-m0-p04-v89.plain_english: And that power is not obstructed by another manifestation merely because another manifestation is absent.

mukta-m0-p04-v90.plain_english: The liberated power is not obstructed, because it is equal to Shiva and there is no further excellence beyond it.

mukta-m0-p04-v91.plain_english: The bonds do not manifest that power, nor is it ever overpowered by them again.
mukta-m0-p04-v91.sanskrit_cite: vyañjayanti na tāṃ pāśāḥ na ca bhūyo'bhibhūyate

mukta-m0-p04-v92.plain_english: The manifestation of what is manifested would last only so long as the manifestor is present.

mukta-m0-p04-v93.plain_english: The Shaiva power that causes manifestation is that very state of proximity.

mukta-m0-p04-v94.plain_english: Thus, for that distinct liberated power, the bonds are not the cause.

mukta-m0-p04-v96.plain_english: Yoga, knowledge, austerity, and activity undertaken as a means to enjoyment.

mukta-m0-p04-v97.plain_english: The mind, because of its insentience.

mukta-m0-p04-v98.plain_english: Even very intense means do not by themselves cause the severing of one's own bondage.

mukta-m0-p04-v99.plain_english: Through connection with a special transformation, that may sometimes somehow occur for someone — thus verse 12.
mukta-m0-p04-v99.sanskrit_cite: pariṇativiśeṣayogāt sa kadācit kasyacit kathañcicca (ślo0 12 ) iti

mukta-m0-p04-v100.plain_english: But when the time of the authority of the obstructing power has passed, it happens of itself for the individual self.

essence: Śiva possesses a nature that encompasses all modes and enables autonomous action
Śiva creates the diverse universe for the enjoyment of experiencing beings
The world’s origin is Śaṅkara, not a material seed like that of a picture
Observed material causes, like thread, are unconscious
The knowledge and action of the great lord cannot be excluded as the cause
mukta-m0-p01.essence_source: derived from argmap inferences (machine-proposed; assessor review outstanding)

essence: Therefore the individual self cannot achieve liberation by its own agency
Therefore the individual self has no power for its own liberation
Therefore neither individual selves nor bonds have the power to effect liberation
Therefore Shiva alone is the giver of liberation to individual selves
Therefore the bonds produce the manifestation of knowing and doing in many ways
